subject: Recap — inference compute strategy & quick wins
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Sullivan <emma.sullivan@brightarc.ai>, Raj Patel <raj@brightarc.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Recap — inference compute strategy & quick wins

Thanks for taking the time today — quick recap so we have aligned next steps. Great discussion; below are the main takeaways, constraints, and proposed near-term actions.

High-level pain points (as described on the call):
- Token/unit economics are increasing month-over-month; your finance team flagged a 3x delta vs initial estimates.
- Tail latency during peak campaigns is causing user-facing stalls (~500–800ms P95 today).
- Burst/seasonal traffic and multi-tenant routing make capacity planning unpredictable.

Current stack (what you said):
- Model: open Llama derivative hosted via HF Endpoints on GCP; single-replica on N1 GPUs for prod, some async batching at the app level.
- Serving: app-level queues implement small micro-batches; no KV/prefix caching at inference layer.
- Observability: basic request logging + Prometheus metrics; limited token-level cost breakdowns.

Success criteria (BrightArc measures this):
- Reduce effective per-1k-token cost by ~35–45% without >5% quality regression.
- Median latency < 120ms and P95 < 250ms during steady-state.
- Predictable capacity plan for 2x peak with clear failover.

Openness and constraints on optimization levers:
- Quantization: you indicated willingness to test int8 or mixed precision in a sandbox, but final production model must pass a held-out QA prompt set.
- Batching: expecting transparent continuous batching at the runtime layer (not app-level workarounds). Target: 2–3x effective throughput improvement for similar latency.
- Caching: interested in prefix/KV cache for common prompts (target 20–30% cache hit to start).

Immediate next steps (owners & timing):
1) BrightArc -> provide 48–72h anonymized token sample and 1 week of peak traffic histogram (Emma) — due by 2026-11-16.
2) Redwood -> run workload analysis and propose config (batching/caching/quant profile) + rough cost delta and canary plan — deliver by 2026-11-19 (owner: me/Neha).
3) BrightArc -> confirm QA/acceptance prompt set and success thresholds (owner: Raj) — target 2026-11-18.
4) Redwood/Legal -> share boilerplate SOW + test access agreement for sandbox quant runs (Monica) — shared draft by 2026-11-17.
5) Canary test: aim for week of 2026-11-23 pending data handoff and environment access.

Attachments referenced: brightarc-inference-snapshot-20261112.csv (sample metrics), call-recording-20261112.mp3.

Open questions we flagged:
- Do you have any hard constraints on model variants we cannot touch (e.g., no LLM rewrites or instruction tuning)?
- Can we deploy a small dedicated pool for the canary or do you prefer hosted integration?

If that all looks right, I’ll kick off the analysis once we get the token sample — happy to sync again mid-next-week for 30m to walk the proposed config.

Thanks,

Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0122

From: Emma Sullivan <emma.sullivan@brightarc.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj@brightarc.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 16:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap — inference compute strategy & quick wins

Thanks Ben — appreciate the clean recap. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- The 3x delta I mentioned is comparing current spend to the budgeted spend for Q3; the absolute spend is still within our runway but line-item visibility is poor.
- We can produce an anonymized token export and a one-week traffic histogram by 11/16. Will remove all customer identifiers before sending.
- On quantization: we are open to int8 experiments but prefer Redwood to run them in a controlled sandbox first (we cannot ship int8 to prod without passing our QA set).
- Regarding dedicated pool: for the initial 2-week canary, we'd prefer Redwood-hosted sandbox (VPC peering ok) to avoid changing infra roles.

Quick ask: can Redwood provide an example JSON schema for the token sample (fields you need) so our infra team can drop it into the pipeline?

We can do a 30m follow-up on Mon 11/16 or Tue 11/17 — morning PT works best.

Emma Sullivan
Head of Platform Engineering | BrightArc
emma.sullivan@brightarc.ai
+1 (628) 555-0199

Attachment: BrightArc_cost_snapshot_Q3.pdf (PDF, 86KB)

Subject: Re: Recap — inference compute strategy & quick wins

Perfect — thanks Emma. Quick answers and follow-up items: 

- Token sample schema: see attached sample_schema.json (CSV/JSON accepted). I’ll also paste the minimal fields below in case your infra team wants the tiny list: timestamp, request_id (hash), model_variant, input_tokens, output_tokens, prompt_hash, latency_ms, region, user_segment (anonymized).
- We’ll plan a 30m sync Mon 11/16 10:30am PT — invite sent.
- Sandbox plan: Redwood-hosted sandbox with VPC peering sounds good. We’ll include quantization runs in the sandbox and gate any model switches behind your QA prompt set.
- Deliverables timeline confirmed: analysis + config by 11/19; draft SOW by Monica on 11/17.

I’ve attached the small example schema as promised and added a one-page checklist our infra team uses for data handoffs. If you want, I can loop in our infra eng (Neha) on the data ingestion thread to accelerate pickup.

Ben

Attachment: sample_schema.json (TXT, 2KB); Redwood-data-handoff-checklist.docx (DOCX, 18KB)
